THE STRUCTURAL FIX, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING DONE TODAY. The four position closes (ACM, ONON, TLT, BCC) were published as recommendations with direction 'sell', position_size_pct 0 and null stop/target. scripts/publish_sheets.py has no concept of a close: positions_from_report() turns every recommendation whose catalyst.wait is falsy into a new PENDING position keyed on (symbol, direction), and merge_report() matches one live position per (symbol, direction). The four open longs are keyed (ACM, buy), (ONON, buy), (TLT, buy), (BCC, buy), so a 'sell' row matches nothing. Simulated against the real state file, merge_report opened FOUR PHANTOM SHORT POSITIONS - ACM at 72.50, ONON at 32.76, TLT at 79.38, BCC at 66.37, each with no stop and no target - while the four longs they were meant to close stayed open. TLT is the worst case: a (TLT, sell) row already exists as a target_hit short opened 2026-09-02, so this would have opened a second TLT short and graded it as a real trade. That is exactly the class of tracker corruption CLAUDE.md's 'How the Performance tab counts' section exists to prevent. The second path was no better: all four carry validation verdict 'fail' on checks that cannot apply to a close (no target, so direction_consistency and risk_reward and stop_distance fail; a catalyst in the past, because the catalyst is what the position was held FOR), and phase 2d --enforce demotes every FAIL to the watchlist and overwrites the note with the failure list. That already happened to BCC on 2026-11-15, where a close instruction was published as 'Demoted by validation: entry or target is missing'. So the choice was phantom positions or a shredded instruction. Both avoided by moving the four to the watchlist with the full instruction intact, which is also the house convention on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16 ('NOT a watchlist idea - an open position to CLOSE AT MARKET'). ALL FOUR CLOSE INSTRUCTIONS STAND AND ARE UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE: close ACM, ONON, TLT and BCC at today's open. They are in the watchlist because the schema has nowhere better to put them, not because they were downgraded. Fixing this properly needs a close/exit concept in positions_from_report and a session guard in the validator, which is a code change with tests and not a 2c edit.

ONE KILL. BJ (was rank 1, conviction 4) on geometry, not on thesis. Fetching 400 sessions instead of 120 moved the whole argument: BJ's 400-day range high is 121.10, so 113.35 is a fifty-two-week high and 111.88 is 7.61% below the 18-month high - not the '1.3% from the all-time high' the key_risk asserted. That puts a real prior high at 121.10 between the 113.60 entry and the 126.00 target. Priced to 121.10 the trade is 7.50 reward against 6.20 risk = 1.21:1 against a 2.0 floor; a shelf measured move (113.35 + 5.75) gives 119.10 and is worse. The published 2.000:1 exists only because the target sits 4.90 points past the only identifiable resistance, and neither 126.00 nor the 133.00 second target is derived anywhere in the evidence - which supplies structure for the entry and the stop and none for the target. A structurally anchored target existed, it failed the floor, and the published target went past it: the target-side version of the stop-walking this repo already refuses. The aggravations (a 2.000 ratio with zero slippage margin on a stop-limit breakout whose fill is not controllable; zero insider buys against $35.6M of sales; a conceded need for a beat-and-raise with earnings inside the horizon) are recorded in the watchlist entry but are not the reason. Two honest ways back are specified there, including a pullback at or below 111.19 with a ~106.20 stop that clears both floors against the 121.10 target.

ONE DISPUTED VALIDATION FLAG, AND I AM OVERRULING IT RATHER THAN HIDING IT. BJ's spread check failed at 25.76% on a Nasdaq bid/ask of 96.23/124.68. That is not a market. The depth record carries is_real_time false and asof 'Nov 16, 2026', the two prices sit -12.8% and +12.9% around the 110.34 prior close, BJ's own 2026-11-16 range was 110.52-111.93, and its 30-day average dollar volume is $208M - a 25% spread in that name is impossible, and the 'round trip costs 236% of the target move' line built on it is meaningless. check_spread has no session guard: when depth is missing it warns 'normal outside regular hours', but when depth is a stale daily record it fails. ACM's 7.37% is a genuine real-time pre-market quote (72.00/77.51 at 06:23 ET) and so is a real but thin book, not an artifact. This did not affect the BJ decision - BJ was killed on geometry and would have been killed with a one-cent spread - but it is logged because a pre-open run will keep failing liquid names on it.

ONE IDEA FIXED AND KEPT. XLV survives at rank 1, conviction 3, 3% - the evidence genuinely rests on two distinct kinds (positioning, technical_level), which is what a 3 means, so the score is paid for and was not moved. But its breadth evidence was materially wrong and has been rewritten. The original claimed the eight largest constituents were all positive over six months and concluded 'the ETF is not a proxy for a single stock that could roll over and take the thesis with it'. The fetched holdings say otherwise: LLY 16.85%, JNJ 10.05%, ABBV 7.61%, UNH 5.34%, MRK 5.32%, TMO 3.78%, AMGN 3.67%, GILD 3.04% - top three 34.51%, top five 45.17%. The list was also not the eight largest; it named BMY, which is 14th at 1.89%, and omitted GILD, which is 8th. GILD is +29.24% over six months so the all-positive count survives, but an equal-weighted count cannot support that conclusion in a fund this top-heavy: LLY returned +13.89% over the past month against XLV's +6.32%, which on current weights is about 2.3 of those 6.3 points, roughly 37% of the one-month move from one stock, and about 7.6 of the 28.93 six-month points. The thesis, key_risk, counter_argument and the evidence detail all now say so, and the holdings URL is in sources. A second concession is now on the record: XLV's 203.50 target has NO structural anchor, because at 187.88 the fund is 2.3% off an all-time high of 192.32 and there is no overhead resistance to measure to, so the 2.22:1 is derived from the stop rather than measured to a level. That is the same objection that killed BJ, and the distinction is deliberate and stated so it can be argued with: BJ had an available structural target at 121.10 and the published target went past it, whereas XLV has none available in either direction. Entry 183.50 (the rising SMA20) and stop 174.50 (below the rising SMA50) are both structural; the target is not, and that asymmetry is the weakest part of the surviving idea. Also noted: PFE and ABT, the two open healthcare positions that put XLV at the correlation cap, are themselves 2.40% and 2.74% of XLV, so the three overlap rather than diversify.

WHAT THE CORRELATION PICTURE LOOKS LIKE NOW. With BJ killed, the BJ/XLV pair the synthesis phase warned about is gone and one new-money idea remains, so there is no longer a pair to size as one. The warning that replaces it is on the exits: closing TLT and closing BCC are the SAME bet, not two - both were long positions that needed the 10Y to fall, so both exits are a bet that it does not. Add the XLV long, which is the defensive side of the same real-rate shock, and the whole report is one macro view. If tonight's NVDA print reignites risk appetite and the long end rallies, the surviving idea and two of the four exits are wrong together. The exits are still right on their own terms - a contradicted thesis and a 90-day unstopped 13% loser - but they are not independent decisions and should not be read as four separate confirmations of one macro call.

recommendations.thesis: Healthcare is the leadership sector of this correction, and that is a measured fact rather than a defensive guess: XLV is +6.32% over one month and +10.69% over three while SPY is -3.05% and -3.58%, giving +9.37 and +14.27 points of relative performance, and it is +28.93% over six months. On 2026-11-16, when SPY fell 1.91% and QQQ fell 2.67%, XLV closed down 0.5%. Participation is broad in count - the eight largest holdings are all positive over six months - but NOT in weight, and the red team corrected the original claim here: XLV is cap-weighted, LLY alone is 16.85% of the fund and the top three (LLY 16.85%, JNJ 10.05%, ABBV 7.61%) are 34.51%, so this is partly a proxy for one stock. It sits 2.3% off its all-time high of 192.32, above a rising SMA20 at 184.26 and a rising SMA50 at 175.37. This is still the right instrument for the view: this report's closed record is 1 of 28 on single stocks at an average -8.3% against 3 of 14 on ETFs at -1.9%, so a sector thesis belongs in the sector ETF rather than in more individual names.
recommendations.key_risk: CONCENTRATION, added by the red team and the reason the original breadth claim was overstated. XLV is cap-weighted: LLY is 16.85% of the fund, JNJ 10.05%, ABBV 7.61% - top three 34.51%, top five 45.17%. LLY returned +13.89% over the past month against XLV's +6.32%, so on current weights roughly 2.3 of those 6.3 points - about 37% of the one-month move - is LLY alone, and about 7.6 of the 28.93 six-month points (26%). An LLY reversal therefore does take a large part of this thesis with it, and LLY is the most crowded momentum long in US large-cap. The original evidence counted the eight largest holdings equally and also mis-listed them (it named BMY, which is 14th at 1.89%, and omitted GILD, 8th at 3.04%); GILD is +29.24% over six months so the all-positive conclusion survives, but an unweighted count cannot support 'not a proxy for a single stock' in a fund this top-heavy. SECOND, the 203.50 target is an extrapolation, not a level: XLV is at all-time highs, so there is no overhead resistance between 187.88 and the target and nothing anchors it - treat the 2.22:1 as an assumption of trend continuation rather than a measured reward. THIRD, the entry requires a 2.3% pullback that may never come - XLV has not traded below 185.36 since 2026-11-09 - so the most likely outcome is no fill at all. That is deliberate; chasing at 187.88 breaks the reward-to-risk floor. FOURTH, a strong NVDA print tonight reverses the rotation wholesale: XLV's 14-point outperformance is partly the mirror image of the AI de-rating, and if QQQ rallies 5% the defensive bid unwinds first. Note also that XLV is the THIRD position on the healthcare driver alongside open PFE and ABT, which is the correlation cap in config/strategy.md, so no further healthcare idea can be added behind it - and PFE and ABT are themselves 2.40% and 2.74% of XLV, so the three overlap rather than diversify.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that +28.93% in six months is not a de-rating being corrected, it is a sector that has already re-rated, and buying a leadership sector 2.3% from its high late in a rotation is buying the crowded hedge at its highest price - the same trade that made XLP and gold look obvious shortly before gold fell 17.8% off its high. That is a real analogue and it is why the entry is a limit below the market and the stop is below the SMA50 rather than a token level: if the rotation is finished, 184.00 trades and then 174.50 trades, and the loss is 2.35 ATR as designed. What the exhaustion argument does not account for is that the relative strength is still widening, not narrowing - the one-month relative gain (+9.37) is running at a faster rate than the three-month (+14.27 over three times the window). Two concessions the red team insisted on, neither of which is answered: the acceleration is itself mostly LLY, which is 16.85% of the fund and ran +13.89% in that month; and the 203.50 target has no structural anchor because the fund is in blue sky, so the ratio that qualifies this idea is derived from the stop rather than measured to a level. The entry and the stop are structural; the target is not, and that asymmetry is the weakest part of the idea.

watchlist.note: RED TEAM KILL (was rank 1, conviction 4). The thesis is fine and the stop is honest; the 2.000:1 that qualified it is not. The entry is 113.60 with the stop at 107.40 (risk 6.20) and the target at 126.00 (reward 12.40). The red team fetched 400 sessions instead of 120 and the picture changes: BJ's range high over 400 days is 121.10, not 113.35, so 113.35 is a FIFTY-TWO-WEEK high and the last close of 111.88 is 7.61% below the 18-month high, not the '1.3% from the all-time high' the key_risk asserted. That puts a real prior high at 121.10 directly between the entry and the target. Priced to that level the trade is reward 7.50 against risk 6.20 = 1.21:1, well under the 2.0 swing floor. The 2.000:1 exists only by placing the target 4.90 points PAST the only identifiable overhead resistance, into new all-time-high territory, inside a 15-session horizon - and 126.00 and the 133.00 second target are round numbers with no derivation anywhere in the evidence, which lists structure for the entry (113.35) and the stop (the 107.60 shelf low of 2026-11-06) and nothing at all for the target. A shelf measured move gives 113.35 + 5.75 = 119.10, which is lower still. So a structurally anchored target existed, it failed the floor, and the published target went past it instead: the target-side version of the stop-walking this repo already refuses. Three aggravations, none of which is the reason for the kill: the ratio is exactly 2.000 at the single highest permitted fill, from a stop-limit breakout order whose fill price is not controllable, so any slippage above 113.60 puts a triggered trade under the floor; insider flow is zero open-market buys against 27 sales totalling $35,591,483 over six months with Form 144s on 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-02; and the report concedes the target 'needs a beat-and-raise rather than an in-line quarter' with earnings on 2026-11-20, inside the horizon. Everything else checked out and is worth keeping: four EPS beats for four, +12.5 points on XLP over three months (share gain, not the sector bid), flat sell-side at 9/9/13/1 unchanged since August, close 111.88 on 1.997M shares against 0.95-1.6M the prior week, ATR14 2.4775, SMA20 108.03 and SMA50 100.32 both rising below price. SEPARATELY, and NOT a reason for the kill: the validation spread check failed BJ at 25.76% on a Nasdaq bid/ask of 96.23/124.68. That is a data artifact, not a market - the record carries is_real_time false and asof 'Nov 16, 2026', the two prices sit -12.8% and +12.9% around the 110.34 prior close, and BJ's own 2026-11-16 range was 110.52-111.93 on $208M of average daily dollar volume. A 25% spread in a $208M-a-day name is impossible; check_spread has no session guard, so it warns when depth is missing but fails when depth is nonsense.
watchlist.trigger: Two honest ways back, both requiring a level rather than a ratio. (1) A decisive break and hold above 121.10, which turns the 18-month high into support and makes blue-sky targets arguable instead of assumed. (2) A PULLBACK entry priced to the 121.10 resistance: at or below 111.19 with the stop at ~106.20 (2.00 ATR, comfortably under the 107.60 shelf) the reward to 121.10 is 9.91 against 4.95 of risk = 2.00:1, clearing both the reward-to-risk floor and the 2.0-ATR stop floor at once. Note this is NOT today's idea - it is a pullback into a print rather than a breakout confirmation, and the report was right to refuse to buy ahead of 2026-11-20 without the breakout, so it is a setup for after the print, not before it. Do not revive the 126.00 target without a derivation.
watchlist.demotion_reason: Reward-to-risk is an artifact of an unanchored round-number target placed 4.90 points beyond the 121.10 prior high; priced to that resistance the idea is 1.21:1 against a 2.0 floor.

Against closing: the entire 2026 rate shock is arguably already in a 25% drawdown, so selling now captures the de-rating with none of the recovery, and a growth scare that pulls the 10Y down is exactly what BCC needs. A cyclical that cannot rally on its own best macro news is not bottoming. Accepted cost: this exits at the low of the range, which is the worst-looking moment to sell and is often the bottom. Taken deliberately - a 90-day position with no stop, no catalyst inside its horizon and a macro driver running against it is a position held by inertia, and inertia is what turned this into -13%.
